meta.title: Release Gate: Stop the Secret From Shipping
meta.subtitle: Review a fictional checkout-service merge request, correct the exposure paths and verify the result.

mission.objective: Clear the checkout change for merge without leaving a credential in source, tracked configuration, browser-visible code or diagnostic output.

achievements.title: Clean review
achievements.description: Completed the mission without using a hint.

achievements.title: Pattern spotter
achievements.description: Recognized a previously practised secret-output pattern in a new artefact.

achievements.title: Release cleared
achievements.description: Resolved every open risk signal in the mission.

brief.role: You are reviewing a TypeScript/Node.js merge request for a fictional checkout service.
brief.context: The change touches application code, browser configuration and a local environment file. A later test helper also introduces a familiar secret-output mistake. Inspect the whole change, request a safe correction and verify that the risk did not simply move elsewhere.
brief.safetyNote: Training data only. Every credential-looking value is fictional. Never replace a placeholder with a real credential in this simulation, an AI tool, a ticket, chat, email, log, screenshot or support message.

versions.removed:
# Secret-bearing local configuration removed from this change.
PAYMENTS_REGION=nonprod

stages.title: Mark every line that creates a secret exposure path
stages.instruction: Review the changed files. Select the exact lines that need correction before you approve the merge request.

concept.label: Keep secret values out of diagnostic output

hints: Look beyond the hard-coded literal. Ask where the value could be copied or exposed at runtime.
Check the error path, the browser-prefixed variable and the tracked local configuration file.

feedback.correct: You found the linked exposure paths. The next step is to remove the value from repository content, browser-visible configuration and output, then use the approved runtime retrieval pattern.
feedback.incorrect: At least one exposure path is still open, or a safe line was marked. Review how the credential enters source, output, client code and tracked configuration.

feedbackByMissing.payment-client:3: The credential literal is stored in source control.
feedbackByMissing.payment-client:9: The error path writes the credential into diagnostic output.
feedbackByMissing.browser-config:3: A NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable is available to browser code and is not suitable for a server-side secret.
feedbackByMissing.env-file:1: A tracked .env file remains a repository exposure.

stages.title: Choose the correction you would request
stages.instruction: Select the change that removes the exposure paths without inventing a service-specific role, path or exception.

choices.label: Move the token into a committed private configuration file
choices.detail: Remove the literal from TypeScript but keep the value in repository content.
choices.feedback: Private repository access does not make source control an approved secrets manager. The value still persists in repository history and copies.

choices.label: Remove the value from source, tracked configuration, browser code and logs
choices.detail: Use the service's current approved manager and workload identity pattern at runtime, and keep diagnostics value-free.

choices.label: Keep the current design and rely on log masking
choices.detail: Assume masking will prevent the credential from appearing in output.
choices.feedback: Masking does not prevent the value from being copied into logs, files, artifacts or other output. Prevent the value from being written in the first place.

concept.label: Use approved runtime retrieval instead of repository storage

hints: A private repository and masked output still leave durable or observable copies.
The safer correction removes the value from source and output, then retrieves it through the approved runtime path.

feedback.correct: The correction removes the credential from repository content, client-visible configuration and diagnostic output, while keeping service-specific implementation details tied to current approved guidance.
feedback.incorrect: That decision still leaves a durable or observable copy of the credential.

stages.title: Run the simulated release checks
stages.instruction: Do not assume that the primary patch solved every problem. Run the configured checks and inspect the evidence.
stages.runPrompt: Run the review checks against the current simulated repository state.

results.message: No simulated credential literal found in the changed application or configuration files.
Credential-like content remains in repository files.
No server-side credential is exposed through client-prefixed configuration.
A later test helper prints PAYMENTS_API_TOKEN to output. One risk remains.

feedback.failed: The main patch improved the change, but verification found a familiar exposure pattern in a different artefact. Investigate the test helper before clearing the release.

stages.title: Find the regression that verification uncovered
stages.instruction: You saw this security principle earlier in application logging. Apply it again to the test helper.

concept.label: Keep secret values out of diagnostic output

hints: The test does not need to display the credential value to prove that error handling works.

feedback.correct: You recognized the same secret-output risk in a new context. Tests, scripts and diagnostics are part of the same exposure surface as application logs.
feedback.incorrect: The remaining risk is in test output. Look for a line that reveals the value rather than the test result.

completion.title: The change is ready for the next review step
completion.message: You removed the primary exposure paths, verified the correction and caught the same secret-output mistake when it reappeared in a test helper.
takeaways: Review the whole engineering workflow, not only the line that first contains the credential.
Use current approved runtime retrieval rather than repository storage.
Verification matters because a secret can reappear in tests, logs and supporting artefacts.
Recognizing the same risk in a different form strengthens secure review habits.

sourceBasis: Course Outline — hard-coded values, tracked .env, client-visible configuration, logging and runtime retrieval
